ATM IV sits at 36.76% — a $84.6 (2.32%) 1σ daily move — with window net GEX at -240.1 and the gamma flip pinned at $2,925, leaving the entire tradable range in short-gamma, move-amplifying territory. five_day_thesis: The real change across five sessions is the vol regime, not the price: ATM IV ran 23.80% → 36.76% (+12.96pp) while spot fell $212.7 (-5.5%) from $3,864.1, and net GEX stayed negative all five days, deepening to -345.6 on 23 Nov before easing to -240.1 on the bounce. The gamma flip slid $3,095 → $2,925 (-$170), so the short-gamma band widened rather than resolved. The structural shift is in near-money call OI: the $3,700 strike went 211 → 1,656 calls (8x, +732 on 24 Nov alone) and $3,650 went 0 → 813 — the first real upside positioning of the window. Against that, the $3,700 put wall eroded 6,070 → 5,690 and the $3,500 put line collapsed 5,169 → 3,323 (-36%), leaving a thinner downside shelf than a week ago. Max pain drifted $5,225 → $5,500 (+$275) purely because spot fell away from static legacy call OI — it carries no directional information.
